claims.text: In BCC refractory high-entropy alloys, toughness retention is governed by the extent of local lattice distortion.
Chemical short-range order controls the extent of local lattice distortion.
Moderate thermal annealing relaxes chemical short-range order.
Relaxation of chemical short-range order diminishes local lattice distortion.
Severe local lattice distortion underpins wavy, high-mobility edge-dislocation behavior.
Wavy, high-mobility edge-dislocation behavior increases the material's capacity to absorb energy before fracture.
NbTaTiV can form a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy after homogenization.
The proposed initial NbTaTiV state is nanocrystalline or ultrafine-grained.
The as-cast or homogenized initial state possesses high chemical disorder and severe lattice distortion.
An intermediate-temperature treatment between 500°C and 700°C can modify short-range order without significant grain growth or precipitation.
The single BCC phase of homogenized NbTaTiV is stable throughout the proposed 500°C to 700°C temperature interval.
Short-range-order-mediated lattice distortion changes the dislocation core configuration.
High-density grain boundaries facilitate plastic flow in the proposed alloy state.
The rough energy landscape caused by severe lattice distortion promotes interstitial-vacancy recombination.
Annealing-induced reduction of lattice distortion makes dislocation motion less effective and thereby embrittles the alloy.
Compared with the as-processed baseline, annealed samples will have lower fracture toughness and earlier crack propagation.
Annealing will shift dislocation slip patterns from wavy, high-mobility behavior to more regular, lower-mobility modes.
Preserved short-range order in the as-processed baseline imparts high energy absorption and plasticity.
